speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked	the Minister for Transport what are the Government's plans to improve the medium- to long-term term reliability of the Bukit Panjang LRT system and what are the immediate- to short-term plans to improve commuter service and experience when there are breakdowns and stoppages in the LRT system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: In the meantime, LTA and SMRT are looking to extend engineering hours to cater to these additional works.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This would mean shorter operating hours and we hope to have commuters’ understanding on this.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The proximity of the new Bukit Panjang Integrated Transport Hub will also allow SMRT to deploy buses rapidly to ferry commuters during a service disruption.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The feedback I have received from my residents in Bukit Panjang Town is that while they are unhappy with the frequent disruptions of BPLRT, they still find that the LRT serves their commuting needs and hope that the LRT will continue as another mode of transport in Bukit Panjang Town.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My first question to the Second Minister is: with this revamp, is there any indication of the timeline, what are the different phases involved and whether there will be disruptions in the process as the operator tries to fix the longer-term problems?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Though this will cause short-term disruptions, we will be providing bus services to bridge any of the inconveniences for the commuters.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In the upgrading process, there will be requirements to secure different parts of the BPLRT.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Likewise, where we can, SMRT will provide the bus services to alleviate commuters' inconveniences.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But because Bukit Panjang is a relatively mature estate, there are limits to how many buses we can put on the roads without causing further congestion.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, we ask for commuters' understanding while we do the short-term and the longer-term upgrades.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The fact that there will be another tender called to revamp the BPLRT means that it is useful.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: My question is: will there be an LRT plan for Yishun Town?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But for the North-South Line, there have been a lot of engineering works done on two fronts.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: One, on the maintenance front, we have upped the reliability to almost 400,000 kilometres before failure.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: This is for the maintenance regime upgrade on the North-South Line.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In parallel, we have been doing a signalling upgrading on the North-South Line.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Things have gone on relatively well, short of a couple of major breakdowns in June and July.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But we are fixing the software issues and, by year-end, we hope to have the new signalling system operating on the North-South Line.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: That will bring better service and conveniences to the hon Member's residents.
